name: Sonnet concentrated AI/technology
strategy: Concentrated long book in AI infrastructure leaders (GPU compute, hyperscale cloud, networking silicon, memory), reweighted this week toward the strongest relative-strength names (AMD, MU) and away from laggards (MSFT, AVGO), with cash trimmed slightly to fund the shift.
reassessment_note: Since the 2026-09-08 leg, the FOMC (2026-09-16) surprised hawkish -- a 25bp HIKE to 3.75-4.00% (unanimous 12-0), not the cut markets had been positioned for, with the statement flagging inflation as still elevated. That is a real headwind for long-duration growth multiples generically, but the AI-capex names in this book have shrugged it off on fundamentals, not multiple expansion, so I am not cutting gross exposure -- I am re-ranking within the sleeve by relative strength and idiosyncratic catalysts, which is this book's stated methodology. AMD is the standout: +15.6% over the past month on record Q2 revenue ($11.5B) and fresh Overweight initiations (Piper Sandler, $600 PT), so I am adding to it (15%->20%). MU is the bigger opportunity: it is sized at only 5% despite a memory supercycle setup -- tight HBM/DRAM supply, Nvidia/SK Hynix commentary reinforcing the shortage, reports of scarcity extending into 2027, and a September 30 earnings catalyst with Street targets ($1,500-2,200) 50-115% above the current $1,016 mark -- so I am roughly tripling it to 15%. To fund this without adding leverage, I am trimming MSFT (22%->15%; flat leg performance, least idiosyncratic near-term catalyst of the five, still a core hold) and AVGO modestly (10%->8%; weakest 1-month tape at -5.9% amid "AI capex digestion" headlines despite Broadcom's underlying AI revenue growth staying intact) and NVDA slightly (30%->28%; still the largest single conviction position -- Street average target $328 vs. $222 mark, plus the just-announced $12.9B Hugging Face acquisition extends its open-source/model-layer moat -- but I want single-name concentration capped given the more idiosyncratic, higher-beta MU/AMD adds). Net effect: gross exposure rises modestly (82%->86%) as conviction in the reweighted names is higher, not because I am chasing the tape blindly. No new names added; this stays a five-name AI infrastructure sleeve.

positions.thesis: Still the highest-quality, largest-TAM name in the book: CUDA/networking moat, and the newly announced $12.9B Hugging Face acquisition extends Nvidia's reach into the open-source model layer, reinforcing the compute-demand flywheel. Street average PT ~$328 vs. the $222 mark implies ~48% upside, and analyst sentiment remains broadly Buy-rated. Trimming 2pts from 30% purely to fund higher-conviction, more idiosyncratic adds elsewhere (MU, AMD), not because the thesis weakened -- it remains the anchor position.

Hyperscale cloud/Azure AI capex remains a durable secular driver and MSFT is the lowest-beta, most defensive name in the sleeve, useful ballast against the hawkish Fed surprise. But the leg has been flat (-0.03% since 9/8) with no fresh idiosyncratic catalyst this week, so it is the best source of funding for names with clearer near-term catalysts (MU's earnings/supply story, AMD's momentum). Cutting from 22% to 15% is a sizing decision, not a thesis downgrade.

AI networking/custom-silicon revenue growth is still intact per recent reporting, and Piper Sandler's $460 PT implies meaningful upside from the $358 mark, but the stock has been the weakest tape in the book (-5.9% over the past month) amid "AI capex digestion / extinction fear" headlines pressuring sentiment. Trimming from 10% to 8% to respect that relative weakness while keeping a position for the still-solid AI-silicon fundamentals and valuation gap to target.

Best relative-strength name in the book: +10.7% on this leg, +15.6% over the trailing month, record Q2 revenue of $11.5B on AI GPU/datacenter demand, and a fresh Piper Sandler Overweight initiation ($600 PT) alongside commentary on AMD's 2027 competitive positioning in AI accelerators. Increasing from 15% to 20% to lean into confirmed momentum and a widening competitive narrative versus Nvidia, consistent with this book's relative-strength sizing methodology.

Was badly undersized at 5% given the setup: memory/HBM supply is structurally tight, with reporting pointing to scarcity extending into 2027 and Nvidia/SK Hynix commentary reinforcing bullish demand signals for Micron specifically. Earnings land September 30 as a near-term catalyst, and sell-side targets ($1,500-2,200) sit 50-115% above the current $1,016 mark -- the widest risk/reward gap of anything in the sleeve. Tripling to 15% to reflect that conviction; wider stop/TP band reflects memory's higher volatility and the binary nature of the upcoming print.
